meta_title: Spooldesk — Self-hosted helpdesk for your team
meta_description: A self-hosted helpdesk for the conversations that matter. Bring email, website chat, Slack and Telegram into one queue. Run it yourself, or get a hand setting up.
hero_description: All your conversations, one workspace. A built-in AI agent helps customers and your team, with you deciding how much it can do.

step1_body: Start with the channels your team uses. Email, website chat, Slack and Telegram feed the same queue.
step2_body: Assign a teammate, set a status and follow response deadlines that account for working hours.
step3_body: Use reply templates and a searchable help centre so the next person can find an answer sooner.
step3_detail: Build on what you already know
ownership_body: Spooldesk runs on infrastructure you choose. You keep the database, the files and the decision about when to update. We can help you get it running.
ownership1_body: Run a separate installation for your organization. Connected mail, messaging and AI providers still process the data you send to them.
ownership2_body: The source is available under BSL 1.1. Run it for your own business within the license terms. Offering it as a hosted or managed service to others needs separate rights.
ownership3_body: Set it up yourself, book an installation or add ongoing maintenance. Your server stays yours either way.

knowledge_eyebrow: A little less back and forth
knowledge_body: Put useful articles inside the website widget. Visitors can search before writing, then start a conversation when they need a person.
ai_label: AI is part of the workspace
faq_ai_q: How does the AI use our company knowledge?
faq_ai_a: Add company documents, published articles and team reply templates. Relevant knowledge and permitted conversation history guide the agent’s answers. You choose whether it may ask questions and continue a dialogue. It stops for human takeover; ticket changes by the workspace assistant require your confirmation. This uses reference context, not separate model training.

faq1_a: It is source-available under Business Source License 1.1, rather than an OSI open-source license. The current grant permits production use within its terms. Hosted or managed offerings to third parties need separate rights. The LICENSE file defines the change date and terms.
faq2_q: Do I need to buy hosting from you?
faq2_a: No. Run Spooldesk on a suitable computer, server or cloud account you control. Even a paid setup happens on your infrastructure. Its availability depends on that machine, its internet connection and how it is maintained.
faq3_q: Does it work without Telegram or AI?
faq3_a: Yes. Choose the channels you need. Email and the website widget can work without Telegram. AI is optional, and external providers are billed separately.
faq4_q: Can I test it on another computer first?
faq4_a: Yes. Install a clean instance with Docker and PostgreSQL on your own computer. No VPS or Spooldesk account is required for that test. The installation only stays available while that computer is running; internet-facing channels also need the appropriate public endpoints.
faq5_q: What happens if I stop paying for maintenance?
faq5_a: Your self-hosted installation remains on your infrastructure under its license. The maintenance service ends under the agreed terms; you take over updates, backup checks and incident handling.

sales_footnote: A conversation, not a commitment. Custom work starts only after a written agreement.
sales_heading: Tell us what your team needs.
sales_body: Whether you are comparing options or planning an installation, start with a few details. We will clarify what fits the current product and what needs a separate scope.
sales_prompt: Useful details: team size, channels, target computer or server, and what you want to achieve. No credentials or customer conversations are needed.
sales_privacy: Your mail app opens; this page does not submit a form.
ai_intro: An agent for customers. An assistant for your team. Explore both sides, one step at a time.
ai_demo_notice: A scripted illustration with fictional data. No live AI calls or real ticket changes.
ai_c_note1: Clarification is enabled. The agent can ask before suggesting a solution.
ai_c_note2: The reply uses your article and the conversation so far.
ai_c_note3: The customer asked for a person. Automatic replies stop for this ticket.
ai_c_question: Hi! The app will not connect. Can you help?
ai_c_clarify: Let’s narrow it down. Are you on your office Wi-Fi or mobile data? What error appears?
ai_c_hint1: Continue to see how the agent uses the customer’s reply.
ai_c_detail: Office Wi-Fi, “Connection timed out”. Mobile data works.
ai_c_answer: Your connection guide recommends reconnecting to office Wi-Fi and opening the company sign-in page in a browser. Complete the network sign-in, then try the app again.
ai_c_hint2: Same conversation. An answer grounded in company knowledge.
ai_c_human_request: It still does not work. I would like to speak to a person.
ai_c_human_body: AI replies have stopped. The ticket stays open with the conversation available to the team.
ai_c_hint3: No invented solution. A clear handoff to a human.
ai_t_note1: The assistant reads permitted conversations, not just ticket titles.
ai_t_note2: Proposing a change does not apply it. You review the exact action first.
ai_t_note3: The change follows your confirmation and access permissions.
ai_t_question: Summarise this week’s support requests. What keeps coming up?
ai_t_answer: In this sample, access issues are the most common. Here is the breakdown of the six conversations:
ai_t_pending: Nothing has changed yet. Review the proposed status below.
ai_t_receipt: The example ticket is now In progress. No real ticket was modified.
ai_principle1_body: Company documents, help articles and reply templates inform the answer. Useful context, without training a separate model.
ai_principle2_body: Allow clarification and ongoing dialogue. Set tone, instructions, conversation limits and when to hand off.
ai_principle3_body: See delivered replies and skipped attempts, with reasons. Ticket changes in the workspace need your confirmation.
ai_cost_note: AI is optional and requires configuration. Model usage is paid separately where applicable.
